Grok Bot turned its night run into an airport departures board, and I've never seen rugs presented this honestly.

You know those old split-flap boards at train stations, where the letters flip and clatter? That's the whole screen. Every coin is a flight. It checks in, gets scheduled, and then either takes off to the moon or never leaves the gate.

The best part is reading the board line by line:

FUDGE · RUGGED · dev rug ×2
SCAMP · RUGGED · honeypot
LURK · RUGGED · vol $4k
MOLD · RUGGED · bundled
ROTT · RUGGED · LP 1 day
GRIME · RUGGED · mint live

Half the flights got cancelled before boarding, every one with a reason. And the ones that did take off:

WHALE to JUPTR · +$2,877
YOLO to NEPTN · +$3,356
APEX2 to MOON-2 · +$2,209
GIGA to MOON-3 · +$1,490

One flight crashed: SKRT to SATURN, REKT -$612.

By 06:00 the bag went from $4,415 to $17,361, 3.93× on paper. 8 out of 10 flights mooned, 80% win rate, and 302 rugs dodged before they ever got a boarding pass.

My honest opinion:

The thing I like most is that cancelled flights stay on the board. Usually trading screens only show you what you bought. Here you see every coin it refused, right next to the winners, with the exact reason written next to it. That's how you actually learn: by looking at what you didn't do.

And the reasons are boring in the best way. Mint live. LP locked for 1 day. Bundled supply. Nobody gets rich by spotting these, but almost everybody gets wrecked by ignoring them.

The part that makes me nervous is the leverage column: 40x, 69x, 88x, 100x, 125x. The board literally says "degen terminal 18+". The one crash, SKRT at 88x, took $612 in one go. The filter is clean. The fuel is way too spicy. I'd keep the check-in rules and fly a lot lower.

Comment "GATE" and I'll DM you the full check-in rules that decide which coin gets cancelled

And tell me: which cancelled flight would you have boarded anyway? I know for a fact I'd have gotten on $WHALE-looking garbage like $LURK just because of the name

Grok Bot treats every trade like a rocket launch, and honestly that's the most accurate metaphor I've ever seen for 100x leverage.

Every coin is a mission. Before liftoff there's a GO / NO-GO poll, and all six agents have to answer: Scout, Filter, Analyst, Grok, Sniper, Guard. Only when every light is green does the countdown start. T-3, T-2, T-1, LIFT. Then the rocket either reaches the moon or blows up on the way.

The flight log reads exactly like mission control:

T-3 $GIGAS poll · all GO
LIFT $GIGAS ape 100x
MAXQ $GIGAS trail armed
MOON $GIGAS +$6,085

And when it goes wrong:

LIFT $DUMPY ape 88x
REKT $DUMPY -$1,218

By mission 9 the manifest looked like this: 6 mooned, 2 rekt, 428 rugs scrubbed before they even reached the launch pad. The mission fund went from $8,820 to $26,630 on paper, 3.02×.

Best flights: $GIGAS +$6,085, $MOONR +$4,733, $WAGMI +$3,968.
Explosions: $DUMPY -$1,219, $BURN -$875.

My honest opinion:

The GO / NO-GO poll is the smartest thing on this screen. Six agents have to agree before anything happens. One NO and the launch is scrubbed. That's 428 rockets that never left the ground, and that's where the real edge is. Most traders don't have a single checkpoint before they press buy. This thing has six.

The trail armed at MAXQ is great too. It means that as soon as the rocket is in the air, there's already a plan to protect the profit. No hoping it keeps going.

But let's be real about the fuel. Every one of those launches ran at 50x to 125x. That's why the explosions are so big. $DUMPY lost over $1,200 in one shot. At that leverage one bad candle is a failed launch, no matter how good the checklist is. The title says 18+ for a reason. If I were running this with real money, I'd keep the six-agent poll and cut the leverage down to something boring.

Comment "LAUNCH" and I'll DM you how the GO / NO-GO poll works and what makes Filter scrub a mission

And tell me: if you had a mission control for your own trades, how many of your launches would have been scrubbed? Half of mine would never have left the pad
